chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man, knowledgeable and meritorious, who died and left upon him a debt that he had been afflicted with, which was not due to corruption, nor extravagance, nor was he known for begging. Would the thousand and the two thousand be paid off on his behalf from the Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Can Zakat money be used to pay the debts of a deceased person?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of Zakat in settling the debts of a deceased believer, emphasizing that the individual must have been a righteous person ('arif faḍil') who did not incur debt through extravagance or habitual begging. The specific mention of amounts (one and two thousand) reflects the economic context of the time and the flexibility of the Imams in applying funds to ensure the deceased's honor and obligations were met. This ruling underscores the communal responsibility to clear the spiritual and financial burdens of the faithful, facilitating their transition to the afterlife.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan and Mihammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about an understanding, meritorious man who dies and leaves debts upon him that he had been afflicted with, not happening by corruption, nor extravagance, nor being well-known for begins. Would these be fulfilled on his behalf from the Zakāt, the thousand and the two thousand?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al- Hassan all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man of knowledge and excellence who dies owing a certain amount of debts. He was not corrupt, a spendthrift, or a known beggar; can his debts be paid from Zakat like one or two thousand? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it can be paid.”
